summary: Assembly is structurally sound. All 203 nodes preserved. 10 edges correctly dropped (orphan/self-referencing tested_by). Two systemic issues require follow-up: (1) inconsistent node schemas across batches (batch-13 uses different field names), (2) 154 nodes have defaulted 'moderate' complexity instead of accurate assessment. One dropped edge is a legitimate data loss from a missing target node.

sections.title: Node Integrity
sections.details: 203 nodes in, 203 out. No node loss. All node IDs are unique. Batch contributions verified: batch-1 (6), batch-2 (9), batch-3 (7), batch-5 (7), batch-6 (35), batch-7 (9), batch-8 (9), batch-9 (9), batch-10 (9), batch-11 (9), batch-12 (9), batch-13 (70), batch-14 (15) = 203 total.

sections.title: Edge Integrity
sections.details: 254 edges in, 244 out. 10 edges dropped: 9 tested_by edges removed because endpoints don't exist as standalone nodes (test↔test or prod↔prod pairs), and 1 edge with missing target (section::docs/specs/_template/domain.md::state-machine → does not exist; correct node is section::docs/specs/_template/domain.md::lifecycle). All 244 remaining edges reference valid node IDs.

sections.title: Prefix Normalization
sections.details: 72 bare paths (e.g. 'docs/specs/...') correctly rewritten to 'file:docs/specs/...' during assembly. 48 edge references rewritten after ID normalization. These corrections are mechanical and correct.

sections.title: Complexity Defaults
sections.details: 154 nodes had null/None complexity and were defaulted to 'moderate'. This affects accuracy of downstream analysis. The majority come from batch-13 (_template files, source code files, and config files) and batch-14 (project-level files). Specific concerns:

items.affectedNodes: All file::* and section::* nodes under docs/specs/_template/
items.recommendation: Re-classify template spec files as 'simple' — they are boilerplate templates with no business logic

items.affectedNodes: file:AGENTS.md, file:README.md, file:app/nuxt.config.ts, file:app/app/app.vue, file:app/public/favicon.ico, file:app/public/robots.txt, file:app/.gitignore, file:.opencode/.gitignore, file:.ua/.understandignore, file:prompts/*.md
items.recommendation: Re-classify: lockfiles (.gitignore, robots.txt, favicon.ico) as 'simple'; AGENTS.md/README.md/prompts as 'moderate' (correct); nuxt.config.ts/app.vue as 'simple'

items.issue: Feature spec files (01-07) correctly 'moderate' but some should be 'simple'
items.recommendation: acceptance.md and test-cases.md specs are tabular/bulleted — consider 'simple'. domain.md, requirements.md, api.md are 'moderate' (correct)

sections.title: Schema Inconsistency (batch-13)
sections.details: Batch-13 uses a different node schema than other batches: {kind, file, label, exports, imports, meta} vs {type, filePath, name, tags, summary, metadata}. The assembler handled this by merging fields, but results in heterogeneous node shapes in the output. Some nodes have 'type' + 'filePath' + 'tags' + 'summary' (from batch-6), others have 'kind' + 'file' + 'label' + 'meta' (from batch-13). Both coexist in assembled-graph.json.
sections.recommendation: Normalize node schemas in a post-assembly step. All nodes should have a consistent shape: {id, type, name, filePath, summary, tags, complexity, metadata}. Map 'kind'→'type', 'file'→'filePath', 'label'→'name', merge 'meta'→'metadata'.

sections.title: ID Naming Convention Inconsistency
sections.details: Node IDs use three different conventions: (1) 'document:' prefix for spec docs (batch-6), (2) 'concept:' prefix for domain concepts (batch-6), (3) 'file::' / 'section::' / 'endpoint::' / 'task::' prefixes (batch-13). Some IDs have double-colon '::' separators, others use single-colon ':'. This is cosmetic but may confuse downstream tools.
sections.recommendation: Standardize ID format: use 'type:path' consistently (e.g., 'document:docs/specs/01-global-table/domain.md' not 'file::docs/specs/_template/domain.md').

sections.title: Dropped Edge Analysis
sections.details: 1 edge dropped with missing target: 'section::docs/specs/_template/business-rules.md::state-transitions → section::docs/specs/_template/domain.md::state-machine'. The target should be 'section::docs/specs/_template/domain.md::lifecycle' (which exists). This is a legitimate fix — the source node 'state-transitions' correctly relates to 'lifecycle' via another edge. No data loss beyond the 9 tested_by edges that were correctly removed (orphan/self-ref).
sections.recommendation: If the state-transitions → lifecycle edge is important, it should be added manually. It is not currently represented.

sections.title: Cross-Batch Edge Verification
sections.details: Import map is empty ({}), meaning no cross-batch edge references were expected or needed. All edges are intra-batch. This is correct for the current batch structure where each batch is self-contained.

sections.title: Feature Coverage
sections.details: All 7 core features are represented: (1) Global Table (batch-6: 35 nodes, 50 edges), (2) Expression Engine (batch-9: 9 nodes, 20 edges), (3) Component (batch-10: 9 nodes, 19 edges), (4) Template (batch-11: 9 nodes, 14 edges), (5) Administration (batch-12: 9 nodes, 13 edges), (6) Document (batch-8: 9 nodes, 13 edges), (7) Render Engine (batch-7: 9 nodes, 12 edges). Supporting infrastructure: batch-1 (project config), batch-2 (architecture docs), batch-3 (design docs), batch-5 (SDD workflow docs), batch-13 (_template spec files), batch-14 (project root files).

sections.title: Graph Connectivity
sections.details: The graph is well-connected. Within each feature (01-07), spec files cross-reference correctly: requirements↔domain↔api↔business-rules↔ui↔ux↔acceptance↔test-cases↔tasks. Cross-feature edges exist via dependency nodes (e.g., ExpressionEngine referenced by GlobalTable and Template). The _template batch forms its own connected subgraph. Batch-1 (config) and batch-14 (project files) are loosely connected via documentation edges.
